title: Counterspy
paragraphs: An espionage and counterintelligence series centered on agent David Harding and his fight against enemy spies, saboteurs, and organized threats to the United States.
Long-running espionage and national-security drama created by Phillips H. Lord.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Blue Network era (May 18, 1942 to June 14, 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], ABC era (June 15, 1945 to August 31, 1950) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], NBC era (October 13, 1950 to September 24, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Mutual era (October 5, 1953 to November 29, 1957) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|mandel-kramer|Mandel Kramer]] (performer), [[person|don-maclaughlin|Don MacLaughlin]] (performer), Phillips H. Lord (producer), Jesse Crawford (organ, organist, and music), Marx B. Loeb (director), Edward Adamson (writer and performer), and Leonard L. Bass (director).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]].

The stories often return to espionage and counterintelligence, robbery, theft and stolen valuables, rackets and organized crime, sabotage, bombs and destructive subversion, smuggling, black markets and untaxed trade, and counterfeiting and financial fraud.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes World War II counterintelligence drama, Postwar and Cold War national-security shift, Broader crime and security cases, and Blue/ABC to NBC to Mutual migration.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|gang-busters|Gang Busters]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], and [[show|crime-and-peter-chambers|Crime and Peter Chambers]].

An espionage and counterintelligence series centered on agent David Harding and his fight against enemy spies, saboteurs, and organized threats to the United States.

Long-running espionage and national-security drama created by Phillips H. Lord.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Blue Network era (May 18, 1942 to June 14, 1945) on Blue Network, ABC era (June 15, 1945 to August 31, 1950) on ABC Radio Network, NBC era (October 13, 1950 to September 24, 1953) on NBC Radio Network, and Mutual era (October 5, 1953 to November 29, 1957) on Mutual Broadcasting System.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Mandel Kramer (performer), Don MacLaughlin (performer), Phillips H. Lord (producer), Jesse Crawford (organ, organist, and music), Marx B. Loeb (director), Edward Adamson (writer and performer), and Leonard L. Bass (director).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to ABC Radio Network, NBC Radio Network, and Blue Network.

The stories often return to espionage and counterintelligence, robbery, theft and stolen valuables, rackets and organized crime, sabotage, bombs and destructive subversion, smuggling, black markets and untaxed trade, and counterfeiting and financial fraud.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes World War II counterintelligence drama, Postwar and Cold War national-security shift, Broader crime and security cases, and Blue/ABC to NBC to Mutual migration.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include Gang Busters, The Chase, Words at War, CBS Radio Mystery Theater, and Crime and Peter Chambers.
